title: Compact weight reader and tokenizer bridge streamline
creator: Lina Zhang
description:
Summary:
We will replace the current monolithic weight deserializer with a compact, streaming Weight Reader and a lightweight Tokenizer Bridge protocol. The goal is to reduce peak loader memory, speed cold-starts for large sharded models, and simplify future format adapters without changing external checkpoint manifests.

Scope:
- Implement a streaming Weight Reader that supports mmap fallback, chunked staged-deserialization, and on-demand tensor materialization.
- Introduce a Tokenizer Bridge (thin protocol) that isolates tokenizer loading from weight ingestion and provides a handshake that tolerates tokenizer version skew.
- Add a migration shim that maps legacy shard layouts to the new reader API without forcing re-upload of checkpoints.
- Update runtime to use the compact reader for model families: llama-variants, opt-family, and redwood-curated opens.

Non-goals:
- Not rewriting the entire model ingestion service or storage layer. Not changing formats on disk for existing customers.

Deliverables:
1) weight_reader_v1 library (C++/Rust bindings) with a documented public contract.
2) tokenizer_bridge module (python/Rust shim) and protocol spec in the repo (docs/tokenizer_bridge.md).
3) Migration shim in ingestion service to register conversion maps.
4) End-to-end benchmarks and perf dashboard changes.
5) Canary rollout plan and migration playbook.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Peak memory per loader process reduced by >= 30% on 7B+ models in standard shard layout during ingestion.
- Cold-start model load time reduced by >= 20% for multi-shard checkpoints (measured median and p95).
- No tokenizer mismatch errors in 99.9% of production requests during 2-week canary with auto-fallback enabled.
- Backward compatibility: legacy manifests load via shim with <= 10% added latency vs native legacy path.

Testing and Validation:
- Unit tests for staged deserialization and tokenizer handshake semantics.
- Integration tests across model families and sharding patterns (N-way shards, interleaved shards).
- Synthetic workload perf harness and real-customer replay for 3 models.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Unexpected tokenization mismatches for models with custom tokenizer binaries. Mitigation: conservative handshake that prefers tokenizer specified in manifest and safelists binary paths; fallback to packaged tokenizer image and alerting.
- Risk: mmap behavior differs across kernels and containers. Mitigation: mmap fallback to chunked file-read; add sysctl doc and runtime flags.
- Risk: Migration shim might miss edge-case manifests. Mitigation: build comprehensive manifest validator and migration dry-run mode.

Rollout plan:
Phase A (dev + bench): implement library, local perf, and unit tests.
Phase B (internal canary): enable for internal-only models and infra team; collect memory/load-time metrics and tokenization mismatch rates.
Phase C (customer canary): enable for low-traffic customer model family with opt-in; monitor and rollback on errors.
Phase D (global): enable by default for targeted model families and publish migration notes.

Observability changes:
- Add metric: weight_reader.materialized_bytes and weight_reader.mmap_fallback_count.
- Add tokenization.health_check and tokenizer_bridge.handshake_latency.
- Dashboard: per-model-family loader memory and cold-start time.

Backward compatibility and customer impact:
- No forced re-upload of checkpoints. Migration shim maps legacy shard naming patterns to new loader semantics.
- Customer impact: low if canary shows success; otherwise fallbacks keep legacy path.
